name: greeble_strip
title: A band of small surface detail (grilles, round plates, tiles, a stud or two) on bricks with side studs, chosen at random from a seed.
why: The busy machine texture on a spaceship hull or a space-station wall, anywhere a flat side looks too plain.

name: engine_nozzle
title: A round engine pointing out of a ship's stern: round plates and bricks built out from a bracket's side studs, ending in a dish with a glowing center.
why: The rear thrusters of any spaceship or rocket.

name: wedge_wing
title: A pair of swept wings from left- and right-handed wedge plates in two layers whose joints cross, so the wings and the deck between them are one stiff plate.
why: The wings of a starfighter or shuttle, wherever the wings have to be part of the hull and not snap off at a seam.

name: angled_hull_panel
title: A smooth tiled panel hung on click hinge plates along a deck's edge and set at an angle.
why: The sloped side, nose, or belly of a spaceship's hull, at any angle the hinges hold.

name: hatch_on_hinge
title: A lid over an opening in a raised floor, on hinge bricks along its back edge, flush when shut or swung open to an angle.
why: A floor or deck hatch on a ship or base: a hold, a ladder well, an engine bay.
note: Uses the same hinge bricks (3937 and 6134) as tilting_hood, as a flush floor lid built apart that opens to any angle.

name: cockpit_canopy
title: A glass canopy hinged at its top to a hinge tile standing on side studs on the wall behind the cockpit, shut or swung up.
why: An opening cockpit for a fighter, a shuttle, or a buggy, where the pilot climbs in under the glass.
note: Uses the older windscreen 4 x 4 x 3 with hinge (2620) on hinge tiles (4625): the modern click-hinge canopies have no usable hinge data in the validator, so they'd never count as connected.

name: turret
title: A gun turret on a 2 x 2 turntable, its head built as one sub-assembly placed at any aim, with bar barrels in round plates on side studs.
why: Gun emplacements on a ship, a base, or a walker, turned to face where the scene needs.

name: radar_dish
title: A 4 x 4 dish on a mast of round bricks, its carrier's handle held in a clip at the top so it tilts to any angle.
why: Radar and comms dishes on a station, a base, or a ship's back.

name: control_console
title: A desk of controls: bricks, a course of 45° slopes as screens, and buttons, grilles, and control-stick levers on the studs along the top.
why: The pilot's or crew's consoles inside a cockpit, a bridge, or a control room.

name: antenna_mast
title: A thin mast from a bar standing in a round brick's hollow stud, with side antennas on bar holders clipped to it.
why: The comms array on a spaceship, a station roof, or a base.

name: solar_panel
title: A pair of mirror-image solar panels clipped onto a bar boom from a side stud, turning together about the boom.
why: Solar arrays on a space station or a satellite.

name: landing_leg
title: A splayed Technic beam leg pinned under a hull, with a foot pinned to its end that stays level, so the ship stands on its pads.
why: Landing gear for a lander, a shuttle, or a walker that has to stand on its own feet.

name: gear_pair
title: Two meshing Technic gears on axles through a pair of Technic bricks, turned half a tooth so they interlock, in ratios 24:8, 8:24, 16:16, 24:24, or 8:8.
why: Any hand-turned or motorized function that needs a speed change or a reversal.
note: Meshing is set by turning the second gear half a tooth; the spacing is real Technic spacing, but the validator only checks that the teeth don't collide.

name: worm_drive
title: A worm gear on one axle turning a 24-tooth gear on an axle across it, in a frame of Technic bricks and plates that puts the axles 5 plates apart.
why: Slow, self-locking turns: a crane's winch or slewing ring, a drawbridge, a turntable that must hold its place.
note: The worm sits 5 plates from the 24-tooth gear, real Technic spacing; the validator only checks that they don't collide.

name: crank_winch
title: A drum of round plates and a round brick on an axle between two Technic bricks, turned by a thin liftarm crank with an axle pin handle.
why: A hand winch for a crane, a tow truck, a well, or a drawbridge.

name: technic_pin_hinge
title: An arm of Technic brick swinging on a friction pin through the hole of a Technic brick beside it, set to any angle.
why: Booms, lids, and gull-wing doors that swing on a pin and stay where they're put.

name: lift_arm_linkage
title: Two parallel Technic beams pinned to a post and to a head, a parallelogram, so the head swings up and down and stays upright.
why: A lifting arm that keeps its load level: a forklift-style lift, a cherry picker, a robot arm, a car wash brush.

name: technic_brace
title: A thin beam pinned across the corner of a Technic brick frame on a 3-4-5 triangle, so both its end holes land on the frame's holes.
why: Stiffening a tall Technic tower, crane boom, or frame so it doesn't rack.

name: rotating_platform
title: A deck of plates and edge tiles built on a 4 x 4 turntable's top as one sub-assembly, placed turned to any angle.
why: A turning base for a crane cab, a radar room, a display stand, or a carousel.

name: ball_joint_arm
title: A chain of 1 x 2 plates with a ball on one end and a socket on the other, snapped together and posed in a curve.
why: A posable robot arm, crane jib, tentacle, or cable that bends at every joint.
